es: Escribir un párrafo largo sobre una decisión personal con conectores variados y recortar frases largas sin perder contenido.

vocabulary.es: es cierto que, hay que admitir que

teaching.en: A wordy sentence can usually be rewritten as a concise version that keeps every idea and loses half the words.
teaching.es: Una frase prolija suele poder reescribirse como una versión concisa que conserva todas las ideas y pierde la mitad de las palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Wordy y concise son opuestos: muchas palabras frente a las justas.
segments: A wordy sentence can usually be rewritten as a concise
version that keeps every idea and loses half the words.
teaching.audioText: A wordy sentence can usually be rewritten as a concise version that keeps every idea and loses half the words.

teaching.en: To tighten up a draft, cut redundant words such as very, really and basically, which add no information.
teaching.es: Para ajustar un borrador, elimina palabras redundantes como very, really y basically, que no añaden información.
teaching.explanationEs: Tighten up = hacer el texto más compacto; redundant = sobra.
segments: To tighten up a draft, cut redundant words such
as very, really and basically, which add no information.
teaching.audioText: To tighten up a draft, cut redundant words such as very, really and basically, which add no information.

teaching.en: Write because instead of due to the fact that, and decided instead of made a decision: each change is shorter and stronger.
teaching.es: Escribe because en lugar de due to the fact that, y decided en lugar de made a decision: cada cambio es más corto y más fuerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Un verbo fuerte (decided) sustituye a verbo + sustantivo (made a decision).
segments: Write because instead of due to the fact that, and decided
instead of made a decision: each change is shorter and stronger.
teaching.audioText: Write because instead of due to the fact that, and decided instead of made a decision: each change is shorter and stronger.

teaching.en: A verbose opening delays the message, so good writers get to the point in the first sentence.
teaching.es: Una apertura verbosa retrasa el mensaje, así que los buenos autores van al grano en la primera frase.
teaching.explanationEs: Get to the point = decir lo esencial sin rodeos.
segments: A verbose opening delays the message, so good writers
get to the point in the first sentence.
teaching.audioText: A verbose opening delays the message, so good writers get to the point in the first sentence.

teaching.en: I trimmed down the paragraph from twenty words to twelve by deleting every superfluous phrase, and no information was lost.
teaching.es: Recorté el párrafo de veinte palabras a doce eliminando cada frase superflua, y no se perdió ninguna información.
teaching.explanationEs: Superfluous es formal: algo que sobra y no aporta.
segments: I trimmed down the paragraph from twenty words to twelve
by deleting every superfluous phrase, and no information was lost.
teaching.audioText: I trimmed down the paragraph from twenty words to twelve by deleting every superfluous phrase, and no information was lost.

teaching.en: Admittedly, the course is expensive; nevertheless, it is worth the cost, because the tutors explain each point clearly.
teaching.es: Es cierto que el curso es caro; sin embargo, merece lo que cuesta, porque los tutores explican cada punto con claridad.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly concede un punto; nevertheless lo contrasta. Los dos conectores varían el ritmo.
segments: Admittedly, the course is expensive; nevertheless, it is worth
the cost, because the tutors explain each point clearly.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, the course is expensive; nevertheless, it is worth the cost, because the tutors explain each point clearly.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión es más concisa y conserva todo el contenido?

choices.text: Because the match was cancelled, we made the decision to stay at home.
The match was cancelled, so we stayed at home.
The match having been cancelled, it was our decision to remain at home.

feedback.es: La versión «The match was cancelled, so we stayed at home» dice lo mismo con la mitad de palabras; las otras conservan frases vacías como made the decision.

hint.es: Busca la versión más corta que no pierde ninguna idea.

origin.text: Original: Due to the fact that the match was cancelled, we made a decision to stay at home.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ahora digo simplemente que decidí dejarlo.»

feedback.es: Decided sustituye a made a decision: un verbo fuerte en lugar de verbo + sustantivo.

hint.es: Verbo en pasado que equivale a «tomar una decisión».

origin.text: Last spring I made a decision to leave my job. Now I simply say that I ___ to leave it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Recorté las frases sin perder ninguna información.»

answer.text: I trimmed the sentences without losing any information
accepted: I trimmed the sentences without losing any information
Without losing any information I trimmed the sentences

feedback.es: Without + gerundio expresa que el recorte no tuvo coste de contenido.

hint.es: Empieza por I trimmed; without losing va al final.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la versión más concisa que conserva todo el contenido?

choices.text: It was essential to finish the important project before the deadline.
It was essential to finish everything we had planned for that week.
It was essential to finish the important project.
Completing the project was absolutely essential before the final deadline date.

feedback.es: Elimina absolutely, completely, basically, very y date, pero conserva lo esencial: terminar el proyecto importante antes del plazo.

origin.text: It was absolutely and completely essential for us to basically finish the very important project before the final deadline date.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué logró la alumna al recortar su introducción.

choices.text: It removed the thesis, which was the most superfluous part.
It kept every idea and respected the reader's time.
It raised her marks, because the essay became much shorter.
It gave the tutor more background to judge her argument.

feedback.es: La alumna redujo la introducción a la mitad sin perder contenido; el texto no menciona ninguna nota ni que se eliminara la tesis.

origin.audio: My tutor returned my essay with one comment: get to the point. My introduction had four sentences of background before the thesis, and two of them were superfluous. I cut them, then replaced due to the fact that with because, and my opening dropped from sixty words to thirty. The content was the same. The essay simply read as though it had been written by someone who respected the reader's time.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión larga con su sustitución más concisa.

pairs.es: Se sustituye por una sola palabra: because
Basta con un adverbio de tiempo

feedback.es: Cada expresión tiene una versión breve: una conjunción, un infinitivo, un verbo fuerte y un adverbio.

pairs.es: Se sustituye por una sola palabra: because
Basta con un adverbio de tiempo

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la narradora sobre su mensaje largo.

choices.text: That the landlord is too busy to read any message about repairs.
That her friend found the long version more convincing than the short one.
That its length hid her request and probably explains the silence.
That an emotional tone always persuades landlords to act quickly.

feedback.es: La amiga le hizo ver que lo que quería (una reparación) se perdía entre tantas palabras; al recortar, el problema se resolvió en dos días.

origin.audio: Last year I wrote an email to my landlord that ran to three paragraphs. I explained, at length and with great feeling, that due to the fact that the heating had broken down, I had been forced to make the decision to move in with my brother. He never replied. When I showed the email to a friend, she asked me what I wanted. A repair, I said. Then write that, she answered. I trimmed the message to four lines, and the heating was fixed within two days. Admittedly, the short version felt less generous to me. Nevertheless, it worked far better.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión ajusta mejor la frase sin perder ninguna idea?

choices.text: She was tired, so she went to bed.
She was extremely tired on account of working long hours, so she made the decision to sleep early.
She was tired after long hours without rest, so she decided to sleep.
She was tired after long hours without rest, so she decided to go to bed early.

feedback.es: Solo la versión «tired after long hours without rest» conserva las dos ideas (horas largas sin descanso y acostarse pronto) con verbos fuertes; «went to bed» pierde información y la otra sigue siendo prolija.

origin.text: She was extremely tired on account of the fact that she had been working for long hours without taking any kind of rest, and she therefore made the decision to go to bed early.

prompt.es: Completa: «El primer borrador era prolijo: repetía cada idea tres veces.»

feedback.es: Wordy describe un texto con más palabras de las necesarias; aquí, por repetir cada idea tres veces.

origin.text: The first draft was ___: it repeated every idea three times. The final version is half as long, and nothing important has been lost.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo sobre una decisión y dos reescrituras concisas (230–290 palabras).

answer.text: Last year I decided to leave my hometown and study in another city. Admittedly, the choice was not easy, because my family lives there and I had never lived alone. Nevertheless, I wanted a course that my local college did not offer, so I got to the point and applied. At first I was homesick, and the flat was small and noisy. However, I soon found friends, and my classes were better than I expected. My parents were worried at first, but they supported me in the end. Looking back, I am glad that I trusted my own judgement, although I still miss my mother's cooking. Long version: Due to the fact that I wanted to save money, I made a decision to work at weekends. Concise version: Because I wanted to save money, I decided to work at weekends. Long version: In order to be able to concentrate, I turned off my phone at this point in time. Concise version: To concentrate, I turned off my phone.
accepted: Last year I decided to leave my hometown and study in another city. Admittedly, the choice was not easy, because my family lives there and I had never lived alone. Nevertheless, I wanted a course that my local college did not offer, so I got to the point and applied. At first I was homesick, and the flat was small and noisy. However, I soon found friends, and my classes were better than I expected. My parents were worried at first, but they supported me in the end. Looking back, I am glad that I trusted my own judgement, although I still miss my mother's cooking. Long version: Due to the fact that I wanted to save money, I made a decision to work at weekends. Concise version: Because I wanted to save money, I decided to work at weekends. Long version: In order to be able to concentrate, I turned off my phone at this point in time. Concise version: To concentrate, I turned off my phone.

Two years ago I decided to change schools, and it was the hardest choice of my life. Admittedly, I was afraid of leaving my friends, and my parents were not sure either. Nevertheless, the new school offered music lessons that my old school did not, so I made up my mind and moved. The first weeks were difficult, because nobody knew me and the timetable was confusing. Even so, I soon joined the choir, and I am happy with my decision today. My parents now say that the move changed my life, and my old friends often visit me. Long version: Due to the fact that the bus was late every day, I had to make a decision to cycle to school. Concise version: Because the bus was always late, I decided to cycle to school. Long version: At this point in time I am in a position to say that I am satisfied. Concise version: Now I can say that I am satisfied.

feedback.es: Un buen párrafo combina una decisión contada con conectores variados y dos reescrituras que conservan el contenido con menos palabras.

origin.text: Cuenta una decisión personal importante con conectores variados (admittedly, nevertheless…). Después copia dos frases largas de tu párrafo y escribe su versión concisa (Long version / Concise version).

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere conseguir Tom con su correo?

choices.text: To persuade Sol to cut repetition without losing ideas.
To ask Sol to replace the headline with a shorter one.
To ask for more examples that support the headline.
To say that the article is too short for the newspaper.

feedback.es: Tom elogia el artículo y pide recortar lo repetido conservando el mejor ejemplo: «You will lose words but not ideas».

origin.text: Dear Sol, thank you for your article. It is interesting, but the second page could be half as long. Several sentences repeat what the headline already says, and two of the stories add nothing. I suggest you keep the strongest example and delete the rest. You will lose words but not ideas. Best wishes, Tom.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una de las dos palabras sobra: es redundante.»

feedback.es: Redundant señala una palabra que repite lo que ya dice otra: plan ya implica futuro.

origin.text: The phrase future plans sounds natural, but the first word is ___, because a plan is always about the future.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El borrador era prolijo, pero cada idea merecía conservarse.»

answer.text: The draft was wordy but every idea was worth keeping
accepted: The draft was wordy but every idea was worth keeping
Every idea was worth keeping but the draft was wordy

feedback.es: Wordy but… contrasta la forma (demasiadas palabras) con el fondo (ideas valiosas): por eso se recorta, no se elimina.
